title: Private chef or restaurant private dining: which is right for your group?
summary: A private chef and a restaurant private room can both make a brilliant group dinner. The right choice...
body_markdown:
A private chef and a restaurant private room can both make a brilliant group dinner. The right choice depends on where you want to spend the evening, how much organising you want to do and what the full cost includes.


Start by picturing the actual night. Will people travel home afterwards, or are you all staying in the same place? Do you want a long conversation at the table without a taxi queue at the end? Is there space at home for everyone to sit down? Answering those questions often narrows it down before you compare a single menu.


> “There’s a different level of intimacy when being part of someone’s celebration as a private chef rather than cooking for parties in a restaurant.”
> —[Chef Charlotte P](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/charlotte-p) , Michelin-trained and former London gastropub head chef ([read her story](https://yhangry.com/why-hiring-a-private-chef-is-worth-it-chef-charlottes-take/) )


### Compare the total cost of the evening


The headline menu price rarely tells the whole story, so compare like for like.


**For a restaurant private room, ask about:**


**For a private chef, check:**


Chefs list what’s included on their profiles. For example:


> “My pricing includes sourcing of top quality ingredients… dishes and kitchen clean up, service by the chef (plus additional servers for parties of 10+), printed menus for each guest, dishes explained by the chef.”
> —[Chef Tom R, Newcastle](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/thomas-r)


Across UK yhangry bookings in the last year, the median price was **£65 per head** . Price per head falls as the group grows: around £69 for 6–10 guests, £59 for 11–15 and £55 for 16–20.


Neither option is automatically cheaper. A dinner at home avoids travel and restaurant drinks markups, but a rented house or hired room is a separate cost. Drinks and childcare are often where the gap shows:


> “It’s great value for money, particularly considering you provide your own drinks and don’t have to pay for babysitters!”
> —[Chef Charlotte P](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/charlotte-p)


#### An example: 12 guests, a Saturday in December, three courses


Restaurant private room (London) Private chef (yhangry, UK)


Food per head £75–£110 (Christmas set menu) £52–£89 (middle half of bookings); median £66


Food for 12 £900–£1,320 £624–£1,068; median £792


Service charge 12.5% on food and drink: £113–£165 Usually included in the quote


Minimum spend £1,000–£5,000+, and December dates can be higher £500-£1,000+


Drinks Restaurant list prices, or corkage of £15–£30+ a bottle where BYO is allowed Your own, at shop prices


Venue Included Your home, or a separate cost if renting


**Total before drinks** **about £1,015–£1,485, subject to minimum spend** **about £625–£1,070**


**How we worked this out:** restaurant figures are typical mid-range Christmas package and minimum-spend ranges for London private dining rooms in 2026, not a quote from a specific restaurant. Chef figures are UK yhangry bookings for 10–14 guests in November and December 2025. Prices vary a lot by restaurant, chef, menu and location, so always compare full written quotes for your own date.


**The main differences:** the restaurant includes the room and the front-of-house team, and it suits guests travelling in from different places. The chef option usually has no service charge or minimum spend, and you can bring your own drinks, but you need the space to host.


### Think about the room


A restaurant gives you an established dining space. Someone else has already sorted the furniture, bathrooms, glassware and service. For some groups, especially large or mixed ones, that’s the main advantage.


At home, you choose the music, the seating and the pace of the evening. You also need a kitchen the chef can work in and a table everyone fits around. Ask whether the kitchen can support the menu while your guests use the rest of the house. Be realistic about seating too. One host described their evening as “last minute change of address, lack of seating and just pure chaos”. The chef pulled it off, but a restaurant would have taken that pressure away.


### Consider menu flexibility


Restaurants often offer a reduced set menu for groups, sometimes with pre-orders weeks in advance. A private chef will usually design a menu around your group:


> “Your relationship with the host starts before the event, honing the menu to something they will really love.”
> —[Chef Charlotte P](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/charlotte-p)


That still takes planning. Ingredients, prep and dietary needs have to be agreed in advance, and almost half of yhangry bookings include at least one dietary requirement. In either setting, explain allergies directly and ask how they’ll be managed. A private setting doesn’t remove the need to check that the kitchen and menu are suitable.


### Think about who’s cooking


In a restaurant, the chef is behind the pass, cooking someone else’s menu. Many yhangry chefs work in, or came from, top restaurant and hotel kitchens.[Chef Jonathan B](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/jonathan-b) , an executive head chef who has worked at Gordon Ramsay’s Boxwood Café, explains why he cooks privately too ([read his story](https://yhangry.com/how-jonathan-a-full-time-executive-chef-cooks-privately-too/) ):


> “You don’t get to put your name on the dish. You don’t get to put your twist on it.”


At a private dinner, the person who made your food is in the room and can tell you about it.


> “That level of interaction and the ability to share stories behind the ingredients is something you can’t really replicate in a restaurant setting.”
> —[Chef Meera A](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/meera-a) ([read more](https://yhangry.com/storytelling-through-senses-private-chefs/) )


If you’d rather the chef stayed in the background, say so. Most are happy to explain each course or leave you to it, whichever suits your group.


### Decide what you want to organise


With a restaurant, your main jobs are collecting menu choices, arranging transport and getting everyone there on time. At home, someone needs to sort drinks, table settings and access for the chef. The cooking and clean-up are handled for you:


> “When you’re in private dining, it’s just you from start to finish — from cooking to cleaning.”
> —[Chef Darek C, Merseyside](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/darek-c) ([read his story](https://yhangry.com/private-cheffing-as-a-side-gig-chef-darek-yhangry-journey/) )


Service is worth asking about if you want help beyond the cooking. Many chefs serve smaller groups themselves and bring staff for bigger ones:


> “For parties of 6+ I always bring a server. For parties of 15+ we typically have 2 servers.”
> —[Chef Luis S, Harrogate](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/luis-s)


Think about the end of the evening too. Restaurant rooms often have a finishing time. A chef booking has an agreed service scope and departure plan, but nobody needs to leave the table afterwards.

### Choose for the occasion


**A restaurant private room may suit you better if:**


**A private chef may suit you better if:**


> “It’s not like being in a city like London or Bristol where there’s endless choice. That’s where hiring a private chef makes a huge difference.”
> —[Chef Caitlin P, Cornwall](https://yhangry.com/booking/chef/Caitlin-p) ([read her story](https://yhangry.com/private-dining-cornwall-caitlin-yhangry/) )


If your space is awkward or your guest list is very large, the practical setup may decide it for you.


> “It felt far more personal and special than going out for dinner.”
> — yhangry customer, 35th birthday for 12


### Compare your options


To compare properly, request a chef quote with your date, postcode, group size and preferred menu. Put the full proposal next to the restaurant’s complete terms, including service charge, minimum spend and drinks, and choose the evening you actually want.

FAQ


Is a private chef cheaper than restaurant private dining?


Not automatically. It depends on the menu, group size and drinks. On yhangry, the median UK booking in the last year was £65 per head, and price per head usually falls as groups get bigger. Bringing your own drinks and avoiding service charges and minimum spends often makes the biggest difference.


What’s usually included in a private chef’s price?


It varies by chef, but often includes ingredients, cooking, serving, explaining the dishes and cleaning the kitchen afterwards. Check each chef’s profile and quote for travel, extra staff and table hire.


Will a private chef serve the food, or do I need waiting staff?


Many chefs serve smaller groups themselves, often up to around 10 guests. For larger groups they usually bring one or more servers. Confirm this in your quote.


Can a private chef handle allergies and dietary requirements?


Yes. Chefs design the menu around your group, and almost half of yhangry bookings include at least one dietary requirement. Share allergies clearly when you enquire and confirm how they’ll be managed.


Are private chefs as good as restaurant chefs?


Many private chefs have worked in top restaurant and hotel kitchens, and some still do alongside private bookings. Check each chef’s profile for their background and reviews.


How many guests can a private chef cook for?


Most bookings are for 6–15 guests, but chefs regularly cook for groups of 20 or more with extra staff. The limit is usually the kitchen and the seating rather than the chef.
